walkthroughs.body_html:
Atoms are tiny, so chemists count them in moles.

1 mole = 6.02 × 10²³ particles. That huge number is called the Avogadro constant.

Whether you have 1 mole of carbon or 1 mole of water, you have the same number of particles.

Ar is the relative atomic mass of an element — you read it off the periodic table.

Mr is the relative formula mass. Just add up the Ar of every atom in the formula.

Example: H₂O has Mr = 1 + 1 + 16 = 18.

Atoms aren't created or destroyed in a reaction — they just rearrange.

So total mass before = total mass after.

That's why equations must be balanced: the same atoms appear on both sides, just bonded differently.

mcqs.q: How many particles are in 1 mole of any substance?
Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
options: To make it look neat
Because mass is conserved — atoms aren't lost or made
Because reactions need equal coefficients
So the products always weigh more

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
